transcript: The other night I attended dig at 59 East 59. Dig is a new play about a woman who's recently moved back to her Ohio hometown to try to heal and put her life back together after the devastating loss of her young son, which everyone knows was her fault and made media headlines all over the country. I was quite impressed with the performances in this play, and although I felt like some of the characters on paper were a little unrealistic, the actors somewhat convinced me otherwise. I also thought the play was really tight, well paced, and had a handful of really moving moments. It's a story of loss, grief, redemption, forgiveness, and although I think it maybe tries to leave you with hope, I thought it was just truly depressing. Which isn't to say I didn't enjoy it, because I did, but just an observation. Dig is running through early November, so see it while you can with that. Another program for my collection.
